title: Stabilising selection
caption: Intermediate values are favoured, so the extremes are removed. The mean stays put but the variation falls and the curve narrows and rises. Human birth weight is an example.
alt: Two bell curves of a trait centred on 50: a dashed curve before selection and a narrower, taller solid curve after stabilising selection.
description: Before: the trait is spread around a mean of 50.
Stabilising selection favours intermediate values and removes both extremes.
After: the mean is still 50 but the spread is smaller, so the peak is higher.

checks.name: after stabilising selection the mean is unchanged at 50 and the peak is higher (0.080, against 0.050 before)
